note: The Highway T campground, the only place camping is allowed on this power-plant cooling reservoir: a built campground on a point on the south side of Route T at the bridge, with concrete pads, a small shelter at each site and fire grates, in two loops. The west loop's three lake-side pads look straight across mown grass to the main arm; the east loop sits back by the road. Boat ramp, courtesy dock and jetty at the foot of the campground. One camping unit and six people per numbered site. The arm north of Route T is a waterfowl refuge. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: one built campground (the Highway T campground), the only camping on the area; concrete pads with shelters in two loops, privy and potable water. Pin is in it. Phone matches. WATERFRONT LEAD upward: three pads 38-45 m from the shore across open mown grass. Owned by Associated Electric Cooperative, run by MDC under lease.
flags: CAMPING AREAS: ONE. The brochure says 'Camping is permitted only at the Highway T campground. Camping is permitted only at numbered campsites... Numbered campsites are limited to one camping or sleeping unit per site. A maximum number of 6 people are permitted in each campsite.' The page says 'The area also has an improved campground with concrete pads, shelters, fire grates, and privies.' The 09/16 map has a single 'Primitive-Individual Camp Sites' symbol, with a Potable Water symbol, on the point south of Route T just east of the bridge (lot H / G area); GIS layer 27 has the one point at 39.62324,-92.61811. The other 16 lots (A-N) carry no camping. No split, nothing 1 km+ away.

ON THE GROUND (imagery, my count, not a published figure, so sites.count not written): a west loop with 10 pads, each with a small roofed shelter, and an east oval with 8 gravel spurs and no shelters visible - about 18 sites. A maintenance yard and two buildings sit between and south of the loops; the boat ramp, dock and jetty are 150 m south-west of the west loop.

WATERFRONT LEAD (stored lakeview; evidence points UP to lakefront): measured from the pads on the 0.22 m/px leaf-off frame. Three west-loop pads are on the lake side of the loop road: about 45 m, 38 m and 40 m from the riprap shore of the main arm, across open mown grass with only a few scattered shoreline trees - no road, driveway or day-use area between pad and water. The other seven west-loop pads are 70-130 m back, inside or behind the loop road with open views. The east loop is 250 m from the lake behind the park road and buildings. So 3 of about 18 pads are on an open apron within 50 m. The reservoir is 4,950 acres. Lakeview is safe as stored; lakefront is supportable for those three - the owner's call.

OWNERSHIP: the page says 'The Thomas Hill Reservoir Conservation Area property is owned by Associated Electric Cooperative Inc. of Springfield, MO... The area is managed by the Conservation Department under a multi-year lease.' The page carries MDC's standard rules (no Rule 101 'not owned' text) and MDC runs the campground, so state stands.
PIN: stored 39.62324,-92.61811 = GIS camping point, in the grass at the north edge of the west loop, 30 m from the nearest pads. No move needed (loop centre is about 39.62270,-92.61810).
ACCESS: directly off paved Route T; gravel loops, concrete pads. Pad length not published; on imagery the west-loop spurs are roughly 12-15 m long.
PHONE: stored 660-785-2420 matches the page's 'For more information call (660) 785-2420'.

SEASON: the brochure gives no camping season (stored year_round, manual, not contradicted). Boating on the main arm north of Highway T is prohibited October 15 through January 15 (brochure); a 'small portion of the area near the power plant' is closed to the public.
